body:
How Likely Is It? (lesson)
1. (a) impossible; (b) equally likely; (c) likely (9/10).
2. P(green) = 3/8, P(yellow) = 4/8 = 1/2, P(purple) = 1/8.
3. 2/6 = 1/3 (rolling a 5 or a 6).
4. 2/5 = 0.4, which is greater than 0.35, so the 2/5 event is more likely.
5. 10/20 = 1/2.

Experiments and Simulations
1. Experimental 29/50 = 0.58; theoretical 1/2 = 0.5. Results vary by chance, especially in a small number of trials.
2. About 50 times: 300 × 1/6 = 50.
3. Red 18/40 = 0.45, blue 12/40 = 0.30, green 10/40 = 0.25. If the sections were equal, each would be near 1/3 (about 13 spins). Red seems to be a larger section, though 40 spins is a small sample, so more spins would help confirm it.
4. 0.70 × 40 = 28 free throws.
5. Answers vary: for example, a roll of 1 or 2 means rain and 3, 4, 5 or 6 means no rain, because 2 of the 6 equally likely outcomes is 1/3.
6. 124/200 = 0.62; 0.62 × 1,000 = about 620 times.

Compound Events
1. H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6: 12 outcomes.
2. H2, H4, H6: 3/12 = 1/4.
3. 3 × 2 = 6 meals; P(tacos with juice) = 1/6.
4. Outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT; at least one head: 3/4.
5. 6 of the 36 outcomes sum to 7 (1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1): 6/36 = 1/6.
6. Answers vary: for example, spin a spinner with 4 equal sections (or roll a number cube and reroll 5s and 6s), each section standing for one card. Count spins until all 4 have appeared, repeat many times and find the average number of spins.

Probability Check (assessment)
1. P(orange) = 3/10; P(not green) = 5/10 = 1/2.
2. Likely (very likely, but not certain). Examples vary: picking a blue tile from a bag of 19 blue tiles and 1 red tile (19/20 = 0.95).
3. 36/120 = 0.3; 0.3 × 500 = 150 times.
4. (1/6)(1/6) = 1/36.
5. BBB, BBG, BGB, BGG, GBB, GBG, GGB, GGG: 8 outcomes. Exactly two girls: BGG, GBG, GGB, so 3/8.
6. A sum of 2 happens only one way (1 and 1), so P = 1/36. A sum of 7 happens six ways, so P = 6/36 = 1/6. The sums are not equally likely outcomes.

Scoring tip: accept equivalent fractions, decimals and percents. On the experiment questions, Advanced reasoning mentions that more trials make the experimental probability closer to the model.
title: Answer key: Unit 6: Probability
